name: North Dakota

notes: Food for home consumption is exempt from state and local taxes; candy, soft drinks, dietary supplements and prepared food are taxed at 5% plus local taxes, which isn't counted here.

Alcohol bought in stores: beer, wine and liquor pay a 7% state gross receipts tax instead of the 5% sales tax, in stores and served, plus city and county taxes, which reach alcohol at their normal rates. Excise taxes paid by wholesalers (16 cents a gallon of canned or bottled beer, 50 cents of wine under 17%, $2.50 of spirits) are left out here.
Drinks served pay the 7% gross receipts tax plus local taxes, and the city or county lodging and restaurant tax where it covers liquor (each such city's page says so).

Cigarettes and other tobacco are taxed at 5% plus local taxes, on a price that includes the excise taxes, which are left out here: 44 cents a pack of cigarettes, 28% of the wholesale price of cigars and pipe tobacco, 60 cents an ounce of snuff and 16 cents an ounce of chewing tobacco. Vapor products pay no excise tax.
Personal care products: children's diapers are exempt since July 1, 2023, which isn't taken out here; over-the-counter medicines and menstrual products are taxed.
Barber and beauty services: haircuts and other personal services aren't taxed: they aren't among the services North Dakota's law taxes.
Laundry and dry cleaning aren't taxed (not a listed service).
Gasoline is exempt from the sales tax and pays a 23-cent-a-gallon motor fuel tax instead, left out here.
Repair labor billed separately from parts isn't taxed; parts are.
Hotel stays pay the 5% sales tax and local sales taxes plus city or county lodging taxes, which aren't counted here.
Motor vehicles pay a 5% motor vehicle excise tax instead of the sales tax (not in these categories); new farm machinery and manufactured homes pay 3%.
gaps: Many North Dakota cities and counties cap their tax on one purchase (Fargo's 2.25% at $56.25, so on the first $2,500; Cass County's 0.5% at $12.50; Grand Forks' 2.25% at $56.25; Bismarck's 2% at $37.50; Burleigh County's 1% at $25; Minot's 2.5% at $150; West Fargo has none; Tax Commissioner, Local Taxes by Location Guideline, October 2026). Shoppers claim the excess back from the Tax Commissioner, or the store charges only up to the cap. Caps are not modeled, which matters little for everyday store sales.

2 cities lie in more than one county with a different rate in each county part; in each census tract such a city's rate is that of its part in the tract's county, counted for the share of the tract's store jobs located in the city.

City and county lodging and restaurant taxes on restaurant meals are counted where the Tax Commissioner lists them (Local Taxes by Location Guideline, October 2026): Beulah 1%, Bismarck 1%, Bottineau 1%, Bowman 1%, Devils Lake 1%, Dickinson 1%, Drayton 1%, Edgeley 1%, Ellendale 1%, Glen Ullin 1%, Grand Forks 0.25%, Hazen 1%, Jamestown 1%, Lisbon 1%, Mandan 1%, McVille 1%, Medina 1%, Minnewaukan 1%, Parshall 1%, Pick City 1%, Regent 1%, Riverdale 1%, Rugby 1%, Valley City 1%, Wahpeton 1%, Watford City 1%, Williston 1%, Wyndmere 1%, Ramsey County 1% (outside cities with their own), Williams County 1% (outside cities with their own). They reach drinks served too, except in Devils Lake, Jamestown, McVille, Wahpeton and Ramsey County, whose taxes cover food only; their lodging part is outside these categories, and Lakota's covers lodging only. Fargo, Grand Forks, Minot, Valley City and West Fargo also collect lodging taxes of their own (not counted).

Seven cities change their tax on January 1, 2027 (Tax Commissioner notice): Arnegard begins a 1% city sales tax; Bottineau, Harvey, Walhalla and Wilton rise from 2% to 3% and Minto from 1% to 1.5%; Harvey and Mandan end their caps on the tax on one purchase. The rates here are current through December 2026; each city's page says so.
